**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "The UK's number one tea subscription" | Unsupported. Superlative/ranking, not on the allowlist, no source. |
| "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time" | Allowlisted. |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | Allowlisted. |
| "Tea Subscription UK" (headline) | Descriptive, fine. |

**Issues**

1. "The UK's number one tea subscription" is an unbacked ranking claim. Nothing in the brand policy supports it, and it would also need a landing page match and likely substantiation under UK advertising rules (ASA/CAP). Remove it or replace it with something allowlisted.

2. Slop-guard check: no banned words, no em-dashes, no exclamation points, no rhetorical openers. Passes. The description does not open with its most useful fact, though: the number-one claim is the opener, and it is the one we can't support.

3. Format note: the headline and description are on one line. Fine for review, but make sure they are entered as separate assets. I did not count characters, as no limit was given.

**Compliant version**

Headline: Tea Subscription UK
Description: Loose leaf and plastic-free tea bags, packed by hand in Bristol. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery over £25.

Claims in the rewrite: "packed by hand in Bristol" (allowlisted), "plastic-free tea bags" (allowlisted), "pause or cancel any time" (allowlisted), "free UK delivery over £25" (allowlisted). Make sure the landing page also states the delivery threshold and the pause/cancel terms.

Verdict: do not publish as written.
